item.title: C/C++ Runtime Endianness Detection Methods Explained
item.description:
“C/C++ Runtime Endianness Detection Methods Explained”

How does one reliably ascertain the byte order (endianness) of the underlying hardware architecture during program execution in C or C++? Various approaches exist, ranging from leveraging standard language features to utilizing compiler-specific macros or networking functions. The goal is to create portable code that correctly identifies whether the system favors little-endian or big-endian representation.

Portable Runtime Checks Using Type Punning and Casting

Several accepted methods rely on inspecting the memory representation of a multi-byte integer. The key is to check which byte occupies the lowest memory address.

item.title: Assembly String to Integer Conversion: In-depth Analysis and Optimization
item.description:
How can I efficiently convert strings to integers and integers back to strings using assembly language, focusing on common x86 architectures and performance?

When working with low-level programming and assembly language, the conversion between string representations of numbers and their integer equivalents is a frequent task. This process requires careful handling of character encoding and arithmetic operations to ensure correctness and efficiency. Let’s delve into how this can be achieved, examining different approaches and optimizations.
